subject: housefly fungus
title: A Fungus Kills Flies at Sunset, Then Uses Their Bodies as Bait

scenes.text: Dead female flies attract more males than live ones.
scenes.keywords: housefly dead on leaf close up

scenes.text: The reason is a fungus. Six days after a spore lands on a housefly, it takes over.
It drives the fly up high to die. In the lab, death comes at sunset.
The corpse fires spores at ten meters a second and gives off a scent males can't resist.
Fresh corpses drew 15 percent of males. Day-old corpses: 73 percent. The males left carrying the fungus.
So yes, the dead ones win. The fungus made sure.

description:
A fungus called Entomophthora muscae kills houseflies and then uses their corpses to lure the next victims.
About six days after infection the fungus forces the fly to climb to a high point and die; in laboratory flies, death comes at sunset. The corpse then ejects spores at up to ten meters per second and releases a scent that attracts males. In a University of Copenhagen study published in the ISME Journal in 2022, 15 percent of males mated with corpses dead for 3 to 8 hours, while 73 percent mated with corpses dead for 25 to 30 hours, and they flew away carrying the fungus.
What other animal has a parasite this cruel?
first_comment: The fungus even runs on a daily clock: its genes cycle with the time of day, which is why death lands at dusk. What's the creepiest parasite you know?
